questions.stem: Hospital engineering reports that the main medical gas piping system has suffered cross-contamination with industrial nitrogen. The anesthesia provider opens the backup oxygen E-cylinder on the workstation. Why must the wall pipeline hose be completely disconnected to prevent delivering a hypoxic gas mixture?
options: Pipeline supply pressure (50–55 psi) exceeds regulated cylinder pressure (40–45 psi), keeping the cylinder check valve closed
The oxygen fail-safe valve closes automatically whenever an oxygen cylinder is opened while pipeline gas is present
Gas flows preferentially from lower to higher pressure according to the principles of electrical impedance
Opening the cylinder while connected to pipeline supply immediately activates the negative-pressure relief valve
questions.explanation: Because pipeline gas enters the machine at 50–55 psi and first-stage cylinder regulators drop cylinder pressure to 40–45 psi, the higher pipeline pressure holds the cylinder check valve closed. The pipeline hose must be physically detached from the wall to allow cylinder oxygen to enter the intermediate system.

questions.stem: During an elective case under general anesthesia, an acute fire flashes inside the patient's oral cavity and endotracheal tube. What two actions must the anesthesia team execute SIMULTANEOUSLY as the absolute first step?
options: Remove the tracheal tube and stop gas flows / disconnect the breathing circuit
Pour cold sterile saline into the airway and activate the hospital pull-station fire alarm
Switch carrier gas to 100% oxygen and extubate the trachea with gentle suction
Discharge a carbon dioxide fire extinguisher into the mouth and close the operating room doors
questions.explanation: Current airway fire management protocols mandate that team members simultaneously pull the burning endotracheal tube from the airway and stop all gas flow by disconnecting the breathing circuit. Saline flushes and ventilation follow.

questions.stem: What is the single most common cause of hypercarbia directly related to anesthesia delivery system management?
options: Failure to turn the ventilator on following successful tracheal intubation and initial verification
Chemical exhaustion of wet soda lime absorbent granules during low fresh gas flow maintenance
Excessive apparatus dead space created by flexible catheter mounts and heat-moisture exchangers
Preferential gas channeling along the smooth internal walls of the carbon dioxide canister
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly highlights that the most common cause of hypercarbia is intubating the patient, confirming bilateral breath sounds and end-tidal CO2, and then forgetting to turn the ventilator on, resulting in unventilated apnea.

questions.stem: How does the ventricular fibrillation threshold for direct current (DC) compare to that of standard 60-Hz alternating current (AC)?
options: It takes approximately three times as much DC as AC to cause ventricular fibrillation
It takes approximately one-third as much DC as AC to cause ventricular fibrillation
Direct current and alternating current have identical thresholds for inducing ventricular fibrillation
Direct current cannot cause ventricular fibrillation because it exhibits zero tissue impedance
questions.explanation: Direct current flows continuously in one direction, whereas alternating current reverses direction at 60 Hz. Because 60-Hz AC repeatedly depolarizes vulnerable myocardial tissue during the relative refractory period, it takes approximately three times as much DC as AC to induce ventricular fibrillation.

questions.stem: Examine the surgical fire triangle diagram below. Which surgical team role is primarily in control of the 'Oxidizer' component?
options: The Anesthesia Provider (controlling delivered O2 and N2O concentrations)
The Operating Room Nurse (controlling flammable prepping solutions and drapes)
The Surgeon (controlling electrosurgical pencils, lasers, and light cords)
The Scrub Technician (controlling moistened surgical laparotomy sponges)
questions.explanation: In the OR fire triad, the oxidizer is controlled by the anesthesia provider via oxygen and nitrous oxide administration. The ignition source is controlled by the surgeon, and fuel is controlled by nursing/OR staff.

questions.stem: Which of the following physical arrangements within a circle breathing system MUST be avoided to prevent accidental rebreathing of expired carbon dioxide? (Select 3)
options: Placing the fresh-gas inlet between the patient and the expiratory unidirectional valve
Placing the adjustable pressure limiting (APL) valve between the patient and the inspiratory unidirectional valve
Placing the reservoir breathing bag between the patient and either the inspiratory or expiratory unidirectional valve
Placing the carbon dioxide absorbent canister in the inspiratory limb on the bag side
Placing the inspiratory unidirectional valve upstream of the patient Y-piece
Placing the expiratory unidirectional valve downstream of the patient Y-piece
questions.explanation: To prevent rebreathing in a circle system, three arrangements must be strictly avoided: (1) fresh-gas inlet between patient and expiratory valve, (2) APL valve between patient and inspiratory valve, and (3) reservoir bag between patient and either unidirectional valve.

questions.stem: How does electrical grounding in the modern hospital operating room compare to electrical grounding in a standard domestic home?
options: In the OR, electrical power is ungrounded while equipment is grounded; in the home, power is grounded
In the OR, electrical power is grounded while equipment is ungrounded; in the home, power is ungrounded
Both electrical power and medical equipment are completely ungrounded in the operating room
Both electrical power and domestic appliances are completely grounded in the home
questions.explanation: In the home, electrical power is grounded to earth potential. In the operating room, electrical power is deliberately ungrounded (isolated from ground via an isolation transformer) to protect against macroshock from spilled fluids, while medical equipment chassis are grounded.

questions.stem: What is the primary operational hazard of an electrosurgical unit (ESU / Bovie) dispersive return pad losing surface contact with the patient's skin?
options: Current density increases over the remaining contact area, risking severe thermal skin burns
Electrosurgical current is diverted through the ECG leads, causing fatal ventricular fibrillation
The machine's line isolation monitor triggers an audible alarm and disconnects wall power
High radiofrequency current passes into the central venous catheter, melting the polyurethane shaft
questions.explanation: The dispersive return electrode safely disperses electrical energy over a wide surface area with low current density. If the pad partially detaches, current density spikes over the remaining contact area, generating excessive heat and severe thermal tissue burns.

questions.stem: According to the American Society of Anesthesiologists Closed Claims Project database, what proportion of total claims involved anesthesia gas delivery equipment?
questions.explanation: In the ASA closed claims database analysis cited, 115 claims out of roughly 6,000 were related to anesthesia gas delivery equipment, representing an overall incidence of approximately 0.23% to 0.4%.

questions.stem: During a total electrical power blackout, the workstation internal backup battery activates. How much operating time does a standard workstation backup battery typically provide, and what occurs when battery voltage drops below ~10 V?
options: Provides approximately 40 minutes (up to 1–2 hours); cuts power below 10 V to prevent deep cell discharge
Provides strictly 15 minutes; maintains low-voltage trickle discharge down to 2 V
Provides 6 hours of continuous ventilation; switches to an internal pneumatic turbine at 12 V
Provides 20 minutes; recharges automatically by converting mechanical gas expansion into wattage
questions.explanation: Workstation backup batteries typically provide approximately 40 minutes (some models 1–2 hours) of electrical power. When voltage falls below ~10 V, the machine automatically cuts power to prevent deep, irreversible battery discharge.

questions.stem: An intubated patient is transported from the OR using a Mapleson A (Magill attachment) breathing system. If the patient is breathing spontaneously, what is the minimum fresh gas flow required to prevent rebreathing of expired carbon dioxide?
options: Fresh gas flow must be at least 0.7 times the patient's minute ventilation
Fresh gas flow must be at least 1.5 to 2.5 times the patient's minute ventilation
Fresh gas flow must equal exactly 3 times the patient's dead space volume
Fresh gas flow must be maintained below 2 L/min to prevent alveolar barotrauma
questions.explanation: For a spontaneously breathing patient on a Mapleson A circuit, fresh gas flow must be at least 0.7 times the minute ventilation, and the corrugated tubing between patient and bag must have sufficient volume to prevent rebreathing. Mapleson B and C require 1.5 to 2.5 times minute ventilation.

questions.stem: Which of the following volatile anesthetic vaporizers CANNOT deliver anesthetic agent during a total electrical power failure once workstation backup batteries are depleted? (Select 2)
options: GE Datex-Ohmeda Tec 6 Desflurane vaporizer
GE Healthcare Aladin electronic cassette vaporizer
Dräger 19.1 Isoflurane variable bypass vaporizer
Dräger Vapor 2000 Sevoflurane variable bypass vaporizer
Conventional mechanical copper kettle vaporizer
Select-a-Tec mechanical manifold variable bypass vaporizer
questions.explanation: Conventional variable bypass vaporizers are entirely mechanical and function on pneumatic gas flow alone during power outages. Heated desflurane vaporizers (Tec 6, D-Vapor) and CPU-controlled electronic cassette vaporizers (Aladin) require electrical power and cannot deliver agent when power is lost.

questions.stem: What are the mandatory standardized fitting dimensions for the single common gas outlet (CGO) on an anesthesia workstation?
options: 15 mm internal diameter (female) and 22 mm external diameter (male)
19 mm internal diameter (female) and 30 mm external diameter (male)
22 mm internal diameter (female) and 15 mm external diameter (male)
30 mm internal diameter (female) and 19 mm external diameter (male)
questions.explanation: Workstation manufacturing standards mandate that each machine has only one common gas outlet, configured with a 15 mm internal diameter (female) and a 22 mm external diameter (male). Conical fittings of 19 mm and 30 mm are strictly reserved for scavenging.

questions.stem: Why does the electrosurgical unit (ESU / Bovie) operate at radiofrequencies between 500,000 and 1,000,000 Hz without inducing lethal ventricular fibrillation when current traverses the myocardium?
options: High radiofrequency current has low tissue penetration and does not depolarize myocardial contractile cells
High radiofrequency current is completely blocked by the patient's skin capacitance
The line isolation monitor converts high-frequency AC into direct current before entering the patient
Electrosurgical units utilize an internal bimetallic strip to ground stray currents to the table
questions.explanation: Standard 60-Hz household current readily triggers ventricular fibrillation. The ESU operates at 500 kHz to 1 MHz; at these high radiofrequencies, current does not excite or depolarize contractile muscle cell membranes, preventing arrhythmias while producing localized thermal cutting or coagulation.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical events can lead to dangerously high pressure within the patient breathing system during spontaneous ventilation? (Select 3)
options: Leaving the adjustable pressure limiting (APL) valve fully closed following preoxygenation
Kinking or occlusion of the conducting tubing between the APL valve and the scavenging interface
Mechanical malfunction or occlusion of the scavenging interface positive-pressure relief valve
Chemical exhaustion of carbon dioxide absorbent granules within the canister
Failure to remove the red protective plug from an auxiliary common gas outlet
Incompetent seating of the inspiratory unidirectional valve disc
questions.explanation: High breathing circuit pressure during spontaneous breathing occurs if the APL valve is left closed, if tubing between the APL valve and the scavenger is occluded, or if the scavenger's positive-pressure pop-off valve fails to open under pressure buildup.

questions.stem: How does the mechanical oxygen ratio proportioning system (hypoxic guard) prevent delivery of a hypoxic gas mixture when nitrous oxide and oxygen are dialed?
options: A mechanical gear chain links the oxygen and nitrous oxide valves to prevent dialing an FiO2 below 25%
A paramagnetic analyzer continuously samples common gas outlet vapor and halts N2O if O2 drops below 21%
An electronic solenoid valve cuts all nitrous oxide flow whenever oxygen pipeline pressure falls below 45 psi
A differential pressure diaphragm injects compressed medical air to dilute high nitrous oxide concentrations
questions.explanation: In traditional mechanical workstations, a physical chain-and-gear link connects the nitrous oxide and oxygen flow control spindles. If the oxygen flow is dialed to less than 25% of the total O2 + N2O mixture, the system mechanically throttles the N2O valve downward.

questions.stem: Under what specific condition will an active mechanical or electronic oxygen ratio proportioning system (hypoxic guard) FAIL to prevent the delivery of a hypoxic gas mixture (<21% O2)?
options: When a third carrier gas such as helium, nitrogen, or medical air is dialed simultaneously
When the pipeline oxygen supply pressure exceeds 55 psig
When the common gas outlet check valve is subjected to positive backpressure
When the volatile anesthetic dial on a variable bypass vaporizer is set above 5%
questions.explanation: The proportioning system only links oxygen and nitrous oxide. If an inert third gas such as helium or medical air is administered concurrently, the proportioning linkage does not account for the additional flow, and a severely hypoxic gas mixture (<21% O2) can easily be delivered.

questions.stem: When performing a morning anesthesia machine leak test, the breathing system consistently fails the automated pressure hold check. What is the most effective and common initial troubleshooting intervention?
options: Swap out the disposable breathing circuit hose assembly for a new circuit
Replace the high-pressure oxygen cylinder first-stage regulator
Disassemble and clean the internal Thorpe tube float stops with alcohol
Depress the oxygen flush valve continuously for 60 seconds to seat the check valve
questions.explanation: The lecture notes highlight that breathing circuit leaks are the most common source of machine check failure. If the leak test fails, swapping the circuit tubing assembly usually resolves the problem.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical statements regarding surgical fire oxidizers in the operating room are correct? (Select 2)
options: Nitrous oxide supports chemical combustion equally as vigorously as 100% oxygen
A mixture of 50% oxygen and 50% nitrous oxide supports combustion as effectively as 100% oxygen
Nitrous oxide is an inert gas that chemically smothers open flames in the oropharynx
High concentrations of medical air accelerate surgical fire ignition faster than pure oxygen
Carbon dioxide gas generated by tissue cautery acts as a potent oxidizer during laparoscopy
Oxidizers can only cause combustion when ambient room temperature exceeds 39°C
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide is not flammable itself, but it releases oxygen upon thermal breakdown and supports combustion equally as well as oxygen. A gas mixture containing 50% O2 and 50% N2O supports combustion as vigorously as 100% pure oxygen.

questions.stem: Following an unresolved airway fire that has been fully extinguished, what is the mandatory risk-management protocol regarding surgical equipment and breathing circuit components?
options: Preserve the entire scene intact, leaving the burned tracheal tube, circuit, and drapes untouched for risk management
Immediately autoclave the breathing circuit and laryngoscope blade to remove smoke toxins
Discard all single-use airway devices in biohazard waste to protect hospital staff from soot
Flush the anesthesia machine manifold with 100% oxygen at 15 L/min for 2 hours before inspection
questions.explanation: Following an operating room fire, the immediate risk management imperative is to preserve the scene completely intact. The endotracheal tube, circuit, drapes, and equipment must not be discarded or altered, as they form the forensic evidence for safety investigations.

questions.stem: A patient transported using a Mapleson B or C circuit requires mechanical ventilation. What fresh gas flow rate must be set to prevent carbon dioxide rebreathing caused by their blind-pouch design?
options: 1.5 to 2.5 times the patient's minute ventilation
0.7 times the patient's minute ventilation
Exactly 0.5 times the patient's minute ventilation
Equal to the anatomic dead space volume per minute
questions.explanation: Because Mapleson B and C systems lack a separate fresh gas conduit between the bag and patient (acting as blind pouches), they permit significant rebreathing unless fresh gas flow is maintained at 1.5 to 2.5 times minute ventilation.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical errors in anesthesia technique account for the vast majority of operating room waste anesthetic gas contamination? (Select 3)
options: Failing to turn off fresh gas flow or flowmeters during tracheal intubation and extubation
Using a poorly fitted face mask or unseated laryngeal mask airway permitting rim leakage
Accidental liquid anesthetic agent spillage onto the floor while refilling a vaporizer
Manufacturing porosity defects located inside the metal vaporizer manifold
Spontaneous recalibration drift of the paramagnetic oxygen sensor
Leaving the backup cylinder check valve open during low-flow anesthesia
questions.explanation: Human error accounts for 94% to 99% of OR gas contamination: leaving flowmeters on when disconnected from the patient, poorly fitting masks/LMAs, unsealed cuffs, and spilling liquid volatile agent (1 mL liquid = ~200 mL vapor).
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety, Slide 17; CO2 and Scavenging, Slide 14

questions.stem: During preoperative workstation inspection, you examine an electrosurgical grounding pad. Modern flexible return pads utilize two separate conductive zones and wiring. What built-in safety function does this design provide?
options: The ESU continuously measures electrical resistance between the two conductive zones and disables the unit if resistance rises
One zone delivers radiofrequency cutting energy while the opposing zone delivers coagulation current
It grounds the operating room isolation transformer to earth ground potential during high current flow
It allows simultaneous use of two monopolar Bovie pencils from a single generator
questions.explanation: Modern split return pads (contact quality monitors) feature two separate conductive zones. The electrosurgical generator continuously interrogates resistance between the two zones; if the pad partially peels off, resistance rises and the unit locks out automatically.

questions.stem: What is the primary mechanical function of the two internal diaphragms connected by a central rod within a workstation cylinder first-stage pressure regulator?
options: Provides negative feedback where outlet gas pressure pushes on the large diaphragm to close the high-pressure inlet valve
Separates oxygen from nitrous oxide to prevent cross-contamination inside the high-pressure block
Converts alternating current into mechanical oscillations that drive the ventilator bellows
Regulates scavenged waste gases into the hospital vacuum line at a steady 16 psi
questions.explanation: In a cylinder pressure regulator, a small diaphragm sits at the high-pressure inlet while a large diaphragm sits in the low-pressure chamber, connected by a rod. As outlet pressure rises to ~45 psi, it pushes the large diaphragm to seat the inlet valve, maintaining constant downstream pressure.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the physical principles of electrical capacitors are correct? (Select 2)
options: A capacitor consists of two parallel conductors separated by an electrical insulator
A capacitor has the ability to store electrostatic charge
In a direct current (DC) circuit, current flows continuously across the insulator indefinitely
Capacitance is measured in ohms and is governed by Ohm's law (E = I x R)
Capacitors are used in anesthesia machines to isolate the patient from high radiofrequencies
A capacitor discharges electrical power exclusively when ambient voltage drops below 10 V
questions.explanation: A capacitor consists of two parallel conductors separated by an insulator (dielectric) and stores electrical charge. In a DC circuit, current flows only momentarily until the plates are charged; current cannot cross the insulator continuously.

questions.stem: If a total operating room electrical failure occurs and backup batteries are depleted, how long does the anesthesia provider typically have to transition the patient to a safe alternative anesthetic (e.g., TIVA and manual Mapleson ventilation)?
options: Less than 1 hour
At least 4 to 6 hours
Exactly 8 hours
Indefinitely, as long as wall pipeline oxygen pressure remains above 50 psi
questions.explanation: The lecture notes explicitly advise that during a complete electrical failure, backup batteries provide roughly 40 minutes to 2 hours of power, and providers should plan to have the patient safely managed under an alternative technique (TIVA, manual bag/circuit) within less than 1 hour.

questions.stem: What is the PISS pin configuration for an Entonox (50% O2 / 50% N2O) cylinder?
options: Position 7
Positions 2 and 5
Positions 3 and 5
Positions 1 and 6
questions.explanation: Under the Pin Index Safety System, Entonox uses a single pin at position 7. Oxygen is 2 and 5; Nitrous oxide is 3 and 5; Carbon dioxide is 1 and 6.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical factors are recognized as primary human-factor contributors to anesthesia equipment-related critical incidents? (Select 3)
options: Inattention and distraction caused by smartphone use or extraneous conversation
Haste driven by operating room turnover pressures
Provider fatigue and circadian disruption
Spontaneous metal crystallization of internal Bourdon tubes
Sudden electrical failure of hospital isolation transformers
Photochemical breakdown of modern volatile anesthetics
questions.explanation: Human error accounts for the vast majority of critical incidents. Aggravating human factors include inattention/distraction (cell phones, conversations), haste, lack of equipment familiarity, and fatigue.

questions.stem: Why is a freestanding positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) valve hazardous if incorrectly placed into the inspiratory limb of an older circle system?
options: It acts as a one-way mechanical obstruction, preventing forward inspiratory gas flow to the patient
It converts laminar flow into turbulent flow, causing rapid desiccation of soda lime
It vents volatile anesthetic vapors directly into the operating room atmosphere
It triggers false-positive alarms on the low-pressure oxygen failure system
questions.explanation: Freestanding PEEP valves are unidirectional. If placed backward or into the inspiratory limb, the valve disc opposes forward inspiratory gas flow, creating a total mechanical occlusion of the breathing circuit.

questions.stem: What mathematical formula represents Ohm's law when applied to alternating current (AC) electrical circuits?
options: E = I x Z (where Z represents impedance)
E = I x R (where R represents ohmic resistance)
P = E x I (where P represents electrical power)
Work = Watts x Time (where Work represents joules)
questions.explanation: In AC circuits, resistance to electron flow is opposed by impedance (Z), which combines pure resistance, capacitance, and inductance. Thus, Ohm's law for AC is expressed as E = I x Z.

questions.stem: During laser surgery of the vocal cords, the surgeon notices a small flame at the tracheal tube. According to fire protocols, what liquid should be poured into the airway immediately after pulling the tube and stopping gas flows?
options: Sterile saline or water
Cold mineral oil
Liquid chlorhexidine
Alcohol-free mouthwash
questions.explanation: After pulling the burning tube and stopping gases, the airway is immediately flushed with sterile saline or water to extinguish residual embers and cool tracheal tissues.

questions.stem: Why is the operating room electrical power supply ungrounded via an isolation transformer?
options: To prevent electric shock (macroshock) if personnel touch a live wire while standing on a wet floor
To allow electrosurgical units to operate without requiring a grounding pad
To prevent high-voltage power surges from melting variable bypass vaporizers
To ensure that workstation backup batteries recharge continuously during surgery
questions.explanation: In an ungrounded system, current is isolated from ground potential. A person standing in conductive fluid (saline/blood) touching a single live conductor will not complete a circuit to ground, preventing macroshock.

questions.stem: What is the primary reason why breathing circuit disconnects occur frequently during head and neck surgical procedures?
options: Surgical drapes conceal the patient's face and airway, hiding accidental tube dislodgement or traction
Head flexion increases apparatus dead space beyond the capacity of the Y-piece
Electrosurgical units generate radiofrequencies that loosen corrugated plastic connectors
Nitrous oxide diffusion softens the 15 mm endotracheal tube adapter
questions.explanation: During head and neck surgery, surgical drapes cover the face and endotracheal tube. Movement of the surgical team or table manipulation can easily dislodge the circuit unseen beneath the drapes.

questions.stem: What type of fire extinguisher is specifically recommended for extinguishing a fire in the operating room when water or saline has failed?
options: Carbon dioxide (CO2) extinguisher
Dry chemical ammonium phosphate extinguisher
Pressurized foam extinguisher
Halon 1211 liquid agent extinguisher
questions.explanation: A carbon dioxide (CO2) fire extinguisher is recommended in the operating room because it leaves no corrosive chemical residue on patient tissues or delicate electronics.

questions.stem: What is the primary electrical hazard of using an electrosurgical unit (ESU / Bovie) on a patient with a permanent cardiac pacemaker?
options: High radiofrequency current can cause electrical interference, resulting in pacemaker reprogramming, inhibition, or myocardial burns at the lead tip
The ESU current causes instantaneous battery explosion within the pacemaker generator
The pacemaker ground wire diverts current, causing the line isolation monitor to trip
Radiofrequency current converts pacemaker pacing spikes into direct current shocks
questions.explanation: The high-frequency energy of an ESU interferes with cardiac pacemakers, potentially causing oversensing (inhibition of pacing), asynchronous resetting, damage to the internal circuitry, or myocardial burns where the lead meets the myocardium.

The ESU current causes instantaneous battery explosion within the pacemaker generator
The pacemaker ground wire diverts current, causing the line isolation monitor to trip
Radiofrequency current converts pacemaker pacing spikes into direct current shocks
questions.explanation: The high-frequency energy of an ESU interferes with cardiac pacemakers, potentially causing oversensing (inhibition of pacing), asynchronous resetting, damage to the internal circuitry, or myocardial burns where the lead meets the myocardium.

questions.stem: During laser surgery of the vocal cords, the surgeon notices a small flame at the tracheal tube. According to fire protocols, what liquid should be poured into the airway immediately after pulling the tube and stopping gas flows?
options: Sterile saline or water
Cold mineral oil
Liquid chlorhexidine
Alcohol-free mouthwash
questions.explanation: After pulling the burning tube and stopping gases, the airway is immediately flushed with sterile saline or water to extinguish residual embers and cool tracheal tissues.

questions.stem: Why is the operating room electrical power supply ungrounded via an isolation transformer?
options: To prevent electric shock (macroshock) if personnel touch a live wire while standing on a wet floor
To allow electrosurgical units to operate without requiring a grounding pad
To prevent high-voltage power surges from melting variable bypass vaporizers
To ensure that workstation backup batteries recharge continuously during surgery
questions.explanation: In an ungrounded system, current is isolated from ground potential. A person standing in conductive fluid (saline/blood) touching a single live conductor will not complete a circuit to ground, preventing macroshock.

questions.stem: What is the primary reason why breathing circuit disconnects occur frequently during head and neck surgical procedures?
options: Surgical drapes conceal the patient's face and airway, hiding accidental tube dislodgement or traction
Head flexion increases apparatus dead space beyond the capacity of the Y-piece
Electrosurgical units generate radiofrequencies that loosen corrugated plastic connectors
Nitrous oxide diffusion softens the 15 mm endotracheal tube adapter
questions.explanation: During head and neck surgery, surgical drapes cover the face and endotracheal tube. Movement of the surgical team or table manipulation can easily dislodge the circuit unseen beneath the drapes.

questions.stem: What type of fire extinguisher is specifically recommended for extinguishing a fire in the operating room when water or saline has failed?
options: Carbon dioxide (CO2) extinguisher
Dry chemical ammonium phosphate extinguisher
Pressurized foam extinguisher
Halon 1211 liquid agent extinguisher
questions.explanation: A carbon dioxide (CO2) fire extinguisher is recommended in the operating room because it leaves no corrosive chemical residue on patient tissues or delicate electronics.
